data.description:
## Why

Evidence recorded on f391-5a20-4593-4405 (resolvable-wavy-avocet), measured by read-only replay of the
persisted REVIEW_RESULT sidecar corpus in this checkout (662 plan-v3 + 1,338 plan-v4 reviews):

1. The G5 deterministic veto (`veto_undecomposed_g5`, `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_lint.py`) fired
   ZERO times across all 2,000 plan-v3/v4 reviews — the `g5_undecomposed_vetoed` coverage key is absent
   from every sidecar, and `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/pass1.py` writes it only when the veto count is
   > 0. It is also barely applicable: only 9.3% (plan-v3) / 8.6% (plan-v4) of reviewed tickets had
   children at all. Yet both the verifier prompt (`src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_verifier.md`)
   and the field description (`src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/verify_models.py`) tell the verifier to grade
   conservatively BECAUSE "a deterministic signal already suppresses false flat findings". That
   justification is not supported by the corpus.
2. Every non-none grade floors impact to 0.85 (`src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/decide.py`), so `low` ==
   `high`. 16 of the 29 recorded fires were graded `low`; in 25 of 29 the undecomposed floor was the
   ONLY hard override present (no dod_uncertifiable, no broken/missing oracle, no contradicts_reality),
   so the floor supplied essentially all of the finding's impact. One `low` grade blocked a plan on the
   floor alone (finding f6dfe0552a79c6e46, ticket ad63-17ad-d545-45d4: impact 0.85, validity 0.7143,
   priority 0.6072 against a 0.60 block line).

This is the same miscalibration already fixed twice: `ac_unverifiable` (ORACLE_GRADE01, plan-v3) and
`divergent_implementation` (DIVERGENCE_GRADE01, plan-v4) were both converted to closed kind sets where
the cosmetic grade contributes below every blocking threshold and never floors. `undecomposed` is the
last ordinal-ladder hard-override axis still flooring on its weakest grade.

## What

- Gate the `undecomposed` hard override on grade: either restrict the floor to medium|high, or convert
  the axis to a closed kind set where decomposition ABSENCE floors and "bundles N independently
  releasable slices" contributes below every block_threshold, mirroring `UNDERSPECIFIED_ORACLE_CONTRIB`
  and `DIVERGENCE_INCOMPLETE_CONTRIB`.
- Rewrite the axis description in `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_verifier.md`,
  `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_verifier_agentic.md` and
  `src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/verify_models.py` so it no longer justifies conservatism by citing a
  suppressor that does not fire.
- Decide separately whether `veto_undecomposed_g5` earns its keep at a measured 0 fires. Do NOT bundle
  its removal into the impact-model change.

## Testing / Verification

- `pytest tests/test_impact_plan.py` — extend it with a case pinning that a `low` undecomposed grade no
  longer reaches the 0.85 floor and that medium|high still do.
- Re-run the read-only sidecar replay used on f391 and confirm the 29 recorded fires reclassify as
  intended. Zero LLM cost, no eval suite, no re-review sweep (ADR 0054).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A `low` `undecomposed` grade no longer reaches the hard-override floor, while medium|high still
      do. Verified: `pytest tests/test_impact_plan.py` passes with the new pinning case.
- [ ] The three prompt/description sites no longer cite the G5 suppressor as the reason to grade
      conservatively. Verified: `rg -n 'deterministic signal already suppresses' src/rebar/llm/` returns
      no matches (exit 1).
- [ ] The IMPACT_MODEL_VERSION bump is batched per ADR 0054 section 4 rather than landed alone.
      Verified: checked by reading the change's commit body, which names the other shape changes it
      ships with.

## Notes

Any impact-model shape change costs an IMPACT_MODEL_VERSION bump that closes the plan-v4 cohort, so it
must be batched per ADR 0054 section 4.
data.title: Retune the 'undecomposed' hard-override axis: gate the 0.85 floor on grade, drop the inert-G5 hedge from its prompt text
